gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-thai: Noto Serif Thai is bookish and authoritative, its bodies dominating the line while ascenders barely show. And Amadeus, rope-like in every stem and bowl, gives it a wide, firm headline to lean on.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-tibetan: Noto Serif Tibetan reads literary and authoritative, with a quiet shift in weight. Amadeus, wide and commanding with strokes like neon glass tubing, sets itself against that brushed-watercolor softness.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-todhri: Noto Serif Todhri reads classic and traditional, with sturdy thin strokes. Its sizable x-height keeps paragraphs easy on a screen, while Amadeus holds its lines at a constant thickness and lets the text carry the nuance.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-toto: Amadeus stretches its words wide across the line, with gaps between curve ends and stems and no hairlines or swells. Noto Serif Toto sets dense, dignified paragraphs in hulking, chalk-pressed lowercase.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-vithkuq: Commanding from the first letter, Amadeus draws its round shapes like bent wire and spreads its words wide. Amadeus makes the statement, while Noto Serif Vithkuqi does the quiet reading work.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-yezidi: Wide and unsparkling up top, with Noto Serif Yezidi tapering gently below. What stands out most is how Amadeus keeps one constant weight while the serif words below settle into solid blocks.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-pt-serif-caption: Amadeus never pinches its curves, and its words run wide. That suits shouting a title, while PT Serif Caption, with its tall x-height and shoulders that thicken gently, does the steadier work of carrying text.
gen-dafont-amadeus-mulish: Approachable and modern, Mulish keeps its strokes uniform throughout. Amadeus does the commanding, stretching wide across the line, while Mulish does the welcoming, with open apertures and a large x-height.
gen-dafont-arkhip-dm-sans: Geometric and modern, Arkhip floats its letters well apart, with a c open like a bent paperclip. DM Sans is friendlier, with wide-set terminals on the s, so a modest size is plenty.
gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-hind: Arkhip floats its letters apart in smooth, uniform strokes. Hind steps in with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals and c endings that never turn inward, so paragraphs move along steadily.
